axisReviews.evidence: Parliamentary competition and constitutional government were retained throughout his second premiership.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: His attempted Communist Party ban qualifies equal treatment of opposition; Indigenous voting exclusions qualify universal suffrage.

axisReviews.evidence: Anti-communist security legislation, censorship and industrial-order policies favoured enforceable public order.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The High Court could invalidate the Communist Party Dissolution Act; security policy did not remove every judicial safeguard.

axisReviews.evidence: The 1949 programme defended cultural homogeneity and White Australia while promoting British-linked national institutions.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Migration expanded from non-British Europe and restrictions eased incrementally; assimilation was not the same as zero migration.

axisReviews.evidence: A large immigration programme for population and development coexisted with racially selective entry.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Labour demand encouraged arrivals, while non-European applicants faced exclusions. A modern housing-based cap is a mixed extrapolation.

axisReviews.evidence: ANZUS, national service and deployments in Korea, Malaya and Vietnam supported allied military capability.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Diplomacy, Commonwealth cooperation and trade with Japan also mattered; autonomous AI weapons have no historical analogue.

axisReviews.evidence: National sovereignty coexisted with Commonwealth and ANZUS commitments.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: His British attachment was cooperative and monarchical, not advocacy of world legislative supremacy. Modern environmental institutions are inferred.

axisReviews.evidence: Private enterprise was preferred while major infrastructure and a national broadcaster remained public.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The Commonwealth Bank remained publicly owned and utilities were mixed; liberalism did not entail selling every public asset.

axisReviews.evidence: Protective tariffs and domestic industry development operated alongside export negotiations.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The Japan trade agreement expanded commerce; protectionism should not be treated as refusal of all international exchange.

axisReviews.evidence: Enterprise, development subsidies and wage arbitration formed a regulated mixed economy.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Public works and tariffs were substantial, but ordinary civilian production was not comprehensively commanded.

axisReviews.evidence: Social security and family support accompanied home ownership, savings and private initiative.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Pensions and means-tested scholarships expanded; this was a safety-net programme rather than systematic equalisation of incomes.

axisReviews.evidence: Non-sectarian civil institutions and religious freedom coexisted with Christian ceremony and support for church schools.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Personal Protestant faith is not evidence for clerical lawmaking or religious family courts.

axisReviews.evidence: His public philosophy emphasised family, monarchy and continuity of inherited institutions.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Higher education and changing economic opportunities expanded; modern same-sex and gender questions are historical extrapolations.

axisReviews.evidence: Snowy Mountains development, Canberra construction, university funding and science favoured technical and material progress.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: These projects do not establish support for embryo enhancement or untested implants; irreversible interventions receive caution.

axisReviews.evidence: Federalism and state institutions were defended within a continuing Commonwealth union.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Commonwealth funding expanded in universities and Canberra; state autonomy was neither secession nor rejection of national coordination.

axisReviews.evidence: Education and personal responsibility were treated as routes to advancement; social formation had an important role.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: White Australia rhetoric and sex-role assumptions are contextual evidence but do not establish a quantitative racial heredity theory. Mixed IQ/race answers reflect that distinction, not invented evidence.
